name: Barbell Glute Bridge (hands on bar)
description: A floor-based hip extension that activates and strengthens the glutes while teaching a strong, neutral-spine lockout. Performed with a barbell.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart.
Brace your core and set the bar across your hips.
Push your hips up toward the ceiling by squeezing your glutes until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Hold the top for a second and feel your glutes contract.
Lower your hips slowly back to the floor. Keep your ribs down and don't arch your lower back.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
description: A glute-dominant hip extension that loads the gluteus maximus hard through a full range — one of the best glute builders. Performed with a barbell.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against a bench and your feet flat, about hip-width apart.
Position the bar across your hips and roll it snug against your hip crease.
Tuck your chin, brace your core, and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor and your shins are vertical.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top for a count of one or two.
Lower your hips under control back toward the floor. Keep the movement in your hips and don't arch your lower back.

instructions: Set up on all fours, on a bench, or in the machine with your spine in a neutral, flat position and your core braced.
Take up the slack on the resistance so there is tension before you start.
Drive your leg back and up using your glute, stopping when your hip is fully extended — don't over-arch your lower back.

Lower your leg slowly under control back to the start, keeping your spine neutral throughout.

name: Barbell Bench Squat
